questions.stem: Real-coded crossover of P₁=2 and P₂=6 generates C₁=0.5(P₁+P₂), C₂=1.5P₁−0.5P₂ and C₃=−0.5P₁+1.5P₂. All candidates are feasible. Retain the two highest-fitness children, first for J(x)=x and separately for K(x)=−(x−1)². Which retained sets are correct?
assumptions: Both stated objectives are maximized separately; all three children satisfy constraints; no elitist parent retention or stochastic selection is added.

questions.stem: A six-bit unsigned chromosome uses endpoint-inclusive mapping x=1+15D/63, with integer code D from 0 to 63. Which code and six-bit string represent the real value x=11 exactly?
questions.subtopic: Binary code versus decoded real value
assumptions: Unsigned binary, most significant bit first; both range endpoints represented; no Gray coding.

questions.stem: Use x=column increasing right and y=row increasing downward. S=(0,0), W₁=(0,1), W₂=(2,4), G=(5,5). Blocked cells are {(1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(4,2),(2,3),(3,4)}. Count unit moves as length L, every entered blocked cell as one collision N, and changes between consecutive nonzero move directions as turns T. Use C=L+10N+T and fitness F=1/(1+C). Decode S→W₁→W₂→G by moving horizontally first and then vertically on each segment. Which (L,N,T,F) is obtained?
assumptions: The complete grid and coordinate convention are transcribed into the stem; boundary waypoints are not double-counted as entries; blocked cells are penalized rather than preventing decoding.

questions.stem: Use x=column increasing right and y=row increasing downward. S=(0,0), W₁=(0,1), W₂=(2,4), G=(5,5). Blocked cells are {(1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(4,2),(2,3),(3,4)}. Now decode each segment of S→W₁→W₂→G vertically first and then horizontally. Which (L,N,T,F) is obtained?
assumptions: Same grid, chromosome, weights and counting rules; ignore zero-length submoves and do not count a waypoint itself as a turn.

questions.stem: A robot receives one sensor vector at a time. Earlier measurements matter, but past vectors are not concatenated into the current input. Which mechanism explicitly carries a learned internal summary from one time step to the next?
assumptions: Sequential inference with state preserved within a sequence; comparisons use exactly the stated inputs and reset behavior.

options.text: An RNN/LSTM whose recurrent state is retained across the sequence.
A feedforward model given only an unordered mean of all measurements so far.
An MLP applied independently to only the current sensor vector.
An RNN/LSTM whose recurrent state is reset before every individual measurement.

questions.stem: A 2-D position belief is Gaussian with μ=(2,2) m and Σ=diag(0.25,0.16) m². Apply deterministic displacement u=(2,1) m with F=G=I and independent zero-mean Gaussian additive motion noise V=diag(0.5,0.4) m². What is the predicted mean and covariance?
assumptions: All position components in the same Cartesian frame; supplied metre units; deterministic control; independent additive Gaussian noise.

questions.stem: For a sufficient state xₜ, observations zₜ and controls uₜ, the source states p(xₜ|x₀:ₜ₋₁,z₁:ₜ₋₁,u₁:ₜ)=p(xₜ|xₜ₋₁,uₜ). Which interpretation is correct?
questions.subtopic: State Markov assumption and belief history
assumptions: x is a sufficient state for the stated controlled model; equality is a modeling assumption, not a claim that every chosen feature vector is Markov.

options.text: Past observations must be discarded from the state belief because the transition model is Markov.
The current control uₜ alone determines the next-state distribution, independently of the previous state.
The latest observation zₜ₋₁ can always replace the previous state xₜ₋₁ in the transition model.
Given the previous state and current control, earlier history adds no transition information; the estimated belief can still depend on past observations.

assumptions: Planar point landmarks; state order robot pose first, then all landmark coordinate pairs.

questions.stem: Use augmented order (x,y,θ,mₓ,mᵧ), with positions in m and θ in rad. Initially μ=(2,1,0,5,4), robot covariance diag(0.04,0.04,0.01), map covariance diag(0.09,0.09), and robot-map cross block zero. The robot moves d=2 m using x′=x+d cosθ, y′=y+d sinθ, θ′=θ. Landmarks remain static. Add independent robot-coordinate noise diag(0.01,0.01,0.0025) after Jacobian propagation, with zero map noise. Which predicted robot covariance and map covariance are correct? (Position variances use m², heading variance rad², position-heading entries m·rad.)
assumptions: First-order EKF covariance propagation; independent additive noise already expressed in robot pose coordinates; static landmark model; zero initial robot-map cross covariance.
